record.name: Mexico
record.summary: No qualifying institute identified. A bill presented on 30 April 2025 would create a National AI Council and an algorithmic audit platform to evaluate data, models and systems for equity, explainability and traceability. The official legislative record lists it as pending in committee.

partial.scope: Negative-status confidence, preserved query provenance, national/official-language search coverage and source-independence audit; this is not a full recheck of all record fields.
Reassessed negative confidence under the revised rule using saved research. No retained English query. No new search or full recheck.
Attempted preservation of cited source copies and checked saved-copy hashes; failures remain in source access notes. This source-evidence work is not a full factual recheck of the record.

English searches for a national AI safety, security or evaluation institute, commitment, proposal or study. English searches did not establish a qualifying institute. Separate follow-up reading of ITSitio (r4-mx-itsitio-bill-lead) identified a proposal for a National AI Council and a National Algorithmic Audit Platform (PNAA), including model and system auditing. ITSitio was opened separately and was not matched to either recorded English query. Its remit requires a separate primary-bill check. The direct ATDT response was a validation challenge. The separate preserved text copy recorded in its source access note was not re-read in this search pass. Partial check only; the last full-check date is unchanged.

Verified the proposed National AI Council and algorithmic audit platform in the Gaceta Parlamentaria of 30 April 2025, articles 7 and 21-23. Added a related body with counts_as_aisi false. The reported July 2026 bill date was not verified; status unchanged. Not a full re-check.
Spanish and English status review, fresh official bill and legislative follow-up, and rereading of preserved ATDT and Gaceta evidence; not a full record recheck.

Aligned current rationale wording with the consolidated capability-or-behaviour-risk test, removing the old severity requirement. This editorial consistency pass adds no research claim and does not change status or the last full-check date.

Checked the bill passage and corrected quotation extraction boundaries, retaining separate support for traceability. The bill remains a parliamentary proposal. This was a partial evidence check, not a full record re-check.

Re-ran searches in English and Spanish for a government-designated institute that evaluates advanced models, or a commitment, proposal or study naming one. No qualifying institute or commitment was identified; results described the ATDT's training and compute work and further parliamentary AI bills, including one in the Gazette of 29 June 2026, which were not opened. The earlier low rating rested on access gaps for later official pages, which the rule does not make a condition. Raised confidence to medium under the status-confidence rule: recorded queries in English and a national or official language, and cited primary governance evidence consistent with no qualifying institute. Partial check; the last full-check date is unchanged.

News search from 17 October 2026 in English and Spanish, with the SECIHTI press room (newest 7 November). No qualifying item was found. The independent AI Safety Mexico body has no retrieved government designation, and a search on the parliamentary algorithmic audit platform did not show adoption or an advanced-model remit. No full review of the legislative docket or of the digital agency's news archive was made. Partial check, not a full record re-check.

check.language_note: The recorded es queries use a national or official language selected for this country-specific check. Other national or official languages were not exhaustively searched. Search source_ids identify registered source URLs matched in the retrieved result set, which may include irrelevant hits. An empty list means no registered source URL was matched, not that the web response was empty. The earlier audit used independent_source_ids for substantive corroboration; governance_source_ids, where present, identifies the selected primary governance evidence. The earlier English-search pass on 17 October 2026 left the then-recorded national or official-language coverage unchanged; the work is described below. The additional status review used Spanish and English searches and read the Spanish primary bill and official legislative record; no primary English bill translation was found. Query source_ids in the additional status review record registered URLs matched in their shared result batch, not attribution to an individual query. Search batches for the additional status review, using 1-based positions in check.searches: 4, 5, 6; 7, 8, 9; 10, 11. Each group records the same exact registered URLs found in its combined search results, without attribution to an individual query. Explicit page opens and finds and unverified URL variants are excluded. Groups list the recorded queries; some requests also contained additional queries retained in the research evidence. On 24 October 2026 the record was searched again in English and Spanish; the result links of each query were matched against registered sources in the same way.
check.independence_note: Historical audit under the superseded two-independent-sources rule: Two substantively independent evidence origins were not established. Multiple pages from one owner, mirrors, reports of the same underlying announcement and general regional coverage are not counted as independent corroboration.
check.governance_note: Primary bill provisions and the official legislative follow-up establish the proposed algorithmic audit platform, which the bill lists as pending in committee. The platform's evaluation concerns equity, parity and explainability metrics, and the reviewed provisions do not establish a remit covering capabilities or behaviour risks of advanced models. The preserved ATDT page describes the government's AI programme of AI solutions for public problems; some later official pages could not be retrieved.

related_bodies.name: Agencia de Transformación Digital y Telecomunicaciones (ATDT)
related_bodies.role: The agency's substantive AI page describes training, public-service AI applications and national supercomputing plans. The reviewed page does not establish a national institute to evaluate advanced models. The saved rendered copy was reread; fresh access failed.

related_bodies.name: Consejo Nacional de Inteligencia Artificial and Plataforma Nacional de Auditoría Algorítmica (PNAA)
related_bodies.role: PNAA would evaluate data, models and systems for equity, explainability, traceability and rights protection as a technical body under the National AI Council. Both bodies are proposed in the bill presented on 30 April 2025. The bill also permits tools for detecting systemic risks. The reviewed provisions do not establish a remit to evaluate advanced models for capabilities or behaviour risks. The retrieved official legislative record lists the bill as pending in committee.

record.notes: The parliamentary bill, sponsored by deputies from MORENA and the Green Ecologist Party, was presented on 30 April 2025, as confirmed by the official legislative follow-up and the Gaceta date in the bill copy held by the Legislative Information System (SIL). No executive sponsorship was established; a parliamentary initiative alone is not the government's own formal proposal under this dataset's rule. This record now uses the primary presentation date, 30 April 2025. The July 2026 date in the secondary lead does not establish this bill's presentation date. Articles 21-23 provide for a technical audit platform, including model and system evaluation, rights-focused metrics and tools for detecting systemic risks. This is relevant model evaluation, but the reviewed text does not establish a national remit covering capabilities or behaviour risks of advanced models. The retrieved SIL record lists the bill as pending in committees of origin; it does not show enactment. Spanish and English searches did not find a later qualifying act. The saved substantive ATDT page describes AI training, public-service applications and supercomputing; the fresh page and one attempt to retrieve a text copy failed. Some later government announcements were also inaccessible, so confidence stays low. The plan's full PDF was not read, and other general AI bills were not individually rechecked.

next_check.reason: Check for an enacted or revised AI bill and any later national AI laboratory or audit-platform mandate covering capabilities or behaviour risks of advanced models.
